annotations.text:
Mobile redesign exploration

Goal: one header instead of two, fewer options in the chrome, and a simpler, more professional feel (Linear / Raycast energy) — while keeping Anchor's language: paper surfaces, white cards, the lime accent, soft shadows.

All four boards show the same Monday with the same items, so only the chrome differs. All values are the real app tokens (oklch), Inter + Source Serif 4.

Current (reference)

What ships today: header pill + week-nav pill stacked (two borders, two shadows), then the canvas panel, then the dock well holding notices, omnibar, and tab bar. Five bordered surfaces compete before any content appears — this is why it reads busy rather than professional.

A — One Bar (leading candidate)

The two headers merge into one pill: identity + date on top, the week strip inside the same surface. Bug report, display options and settings collapse behind one ... menu; the layout picker becomes a small segmented control next to the content it switches. Dock unchanged.

Why: the lowest-risk consolidation — reclaims ~40px and removes two of the five competing surfaces without touching navigation or capture.
Tradeoff: still a chrome-heavy app; the dock well remains the heaviest element on screen.

B — Command Deck

Raycast-inspired: chrome nearly disappears. Title and a bare day strip sit straight on paper, content becomes one full-bleed sheet with hairline sections instead of nested cards, and a single bottom capsule owns everything — tab icons, capture ('type to add or command'), and Beacon.

Why: maximal content per screen and the strongest 'powerful tool' feel; one bar is the whole command surface.
Tradeoff: biggest departure — buckets lose their card identity, notices need a new home, and folding chat behind the Beacon button is a navigation change.

C — Editorial Calm

Typography-led quiet: a Source Serif 'Today' headline (the brand's own serif) on bare paper, a numeral day strip with a lime dot, bucket cards floating directly on the backdrop, and an icons-only tab row. Capture moves to a floating lime button that opens the omnibar as a sheet.

Why: the calmest, most 'designed' feel — hierarchy comes from type and spacing, and the cards finally read as the heroes.
Tradeoff: capture is one tap farther away than the always-present omnibar, and the dock's one-voice notice stack loses its anchor.
